query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for high-temperature and irradiation-exposed applications, what intervention could improve mechanical performance while maintaining thermal and irradiation stability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 2 at.% Ti and 1 at.% B to the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy will improve its mechanical performance by 20% increase in yield strength and 15% improvement in ductility compared to the baseline alloy, while maintaining thermal and irradiation stability.
generation.intervention: Addition of 2 at.% Ti and 1 at.% B
generation.conditions: Annealing at 1000°C for 24 hours, followed by irradiation with 3 MeV Au ions to a dose of 10 dpa at 500°C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of Ti-rich precipitates and B segregation to grain boundaries
generation.mechanism: The Ti-rich precipitates act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects, while B segregation enhances grain boundary cohesion, leading to improved mechanical performance and stability
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in yield strength and 15% improvement in ductility compared to the baseline AlCoCrFeNi alloy, while maintaining thermal and irradiation stability
